Talking About Yourself

Answer questions about your home, your work and your plans with full sentences, reasons and examples — the complete IELTS Speaking test.

Exam focus: Speaking Parts 1–3

Grammar

Talking about yourself

12 min

A · Present simple: facts and routines

I / you / we / theyhe / she / it
+I work in a hospital.She works in a hospital.
–I don't like cold weather.He doesn't like cold weather.
?Do you live in a flat?Does your wife work?
Exercise 1

Choose the correct form.

  1. My brother ______ in a hospital.
  2. ______ you live in a flat?
  3. She ______ like cold weather.
  4. I usually ______ work at 7 am.
  5. What ______ your wife do?
  6. We ______ near the city centre.

B · Likes and wishes

like / love / enjoy / hate + -ing

I enjoy cooking. · She loves walking by the sea. · I don't like getting up early.

would like + to + verb

I'd like to live near the sea. · I'd like to improve my English. · (= I want, but more polite)

Exercise 2

Choose the correct form.

  1. I enjoy ______ for my family.
  2. I would like ______ in a bigger flat.
  3. She loves ______ by the sea.
  4. I'd like ______ my English.
  5. I don't like ______ up early.

C · Longer answers: Answer + Reason + Example

1 · Answer

Yes, I do. / Not really.

2 · Reason

…because every day is different.

3 · Example

For example, yesterday I worked in a school.

Vocabulary + pronunciation

Work, places and feelings

10 min

Study the 12 words. Press 🔈 to hear each word and the example sentence.

colleaguenoun
A person you work with.
My colleagues are very friendly.
shiftnoun
The hours you work, for example 6 am to 2 pm.
I work the night shift on Fridays.
full-time / part-timeadjective
Full-time: about 35–40 hours a week. Part-time: fewer hours.
I have a full-time job.
hometownnoun
The town or city where you were born or grew up.
My hometown is São Paulo.
busyadjective
With a lot of people, cars or activity.
The city centre is always busy.
crowdedadjective
Too full of people.
The buses are crowded in the morning.
quietadjective
With little noise.
My street is quiet at night.
peacefuladjective
Calm and relaxing.
The countryside is peaceful.
modernadjective
New, using new ideas or designs.
Our office is in a modern building.
historicadjective
Old and important in history.
York is a historic city.
excitedadjective
Very happy about something in the future.
I'm excited about my new job.
homesickadjective
Sad because you miss your home and family.
Sometimes I feel homesick.

Exam strategy

How to do well in each part

8 min
Part 1

2–3 sentences per answer

Answer + Reason + Example. Don't learn answers by heart — examiners notice, and it lowers your score.

Part 2

Use the minute to make notes

Write 2–3 key words for each line of the card. Talk about every line. Keep going until the examiner stops you.

Part 3

Opinion + reason + both sides

"I think… because…" · "It depends on…" · "On the other hand…". Longer answers are better here.

Describe a place where you would like to live in the future.

You should say:
  • where it is
  • what it is like
  • who you would live there with
and explain why you would like to live there.

A Part 2 task card — the same topic as today's mock exam.

Exercise 6

Which notes are the best?

You have one minute to make notes for this card. Which notes are best?

The best notes have key words for every line of the card. Notes A forget "who" and "why"; B is a full sentence — there is no time to write sentences.
Exercise 7

Useful phrases: what does each one do?

  1. "That's an interesting question. Let me think…"
  2. "For example, in my city…"
  3. "It depends on your age."
  4. "Personally, I think…"
  5. "Sorry, could you repeat the question, please?"

Practice test

IELTS Speaking · full test

Time: 11–14 minutes · Use headphones and a quiet room.

  1. The examiner asks a question. Answer out loud, then press Next question.
  2. In Part 2 you get 1 minute to prepare (make notes on paper) and up to 2 minutes to speak.
  3. Your whole test is recorded. At the end you can listen to it and download it for your teacher.
  4. Allow the microphone when your browser asks.

Examiner · Helen Carter
…

Describe a place where you would like to live in the future.

You should say:
  • where it is
  • what it is like
  • who you would live there with
and explain why you would like to live there.
Good afternoon. My name is Helen Carter. Can you tell me your full name, please?
And what shall I call you?
And can you tell me where you're from?
Now, in this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about what you do. Do you work or are you a student?
What do you do in your job?
What do you like about your job?
Now let's talk about where you live. Do you live in a house or a flat?
Which is your favourite room? Why?
What would you like to change about your home?
Let's move on to talk about cooking. How often do you cook?
What kind of food do you like to cook?
Now I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here's your topic: describe a place where you would like to live in the future.
Alright? Remember you have one to two minutes for this, so don't worry if I stop you. I'll tell you when the time is up. Can you start speaking now, please?
Thank you. Do you think you will really live there one day?
We've been talking about a place you'd like to live. Let's consider first of all moving to another country. Why do people move to other countries to work?
What problems can people have when they move to a new country?
Is it better to live in a city or in the countryside? Why?
Finally, let's talk about housing. Do you think it's easy for young people to buy a home today?
Thank you. That is the end of the speaking test.
Exam script

A full Speaking test — examiner and candidate

Lucas, an electrician from Brazil, takes the test. His answers are at about Band 6 — a little above the visa target, so a good model to aim for. Listen, read, and turn on the teacher notes to see what makes each answer good.

Marking guide

How Speaking is marked

The examiner gives a band for each of four criteria, each worth 25%. Below is a simplified guide for bands 4–7 — see the official public band descriptors on ielts.org for the full wording.

BandFluency & coherenceVocabularyGrammarPronunciation
7Speaks at length without effort; some hesitation; good linking.Flexible; some less common words and phrases.A range of complex sentences; frequent error-free sentences.Easy to understand; good stress and intonation.
6Willing to speak at length; some repetition or self-correction.Enough words to discuss topics; can paraphrase.Simple and complex sentences; errors rarely block meaning.Generally clear; some sounds or stress unclear at times.
5Keeps going but slowly; repeats; simple linking.Manages familiar topics; limited for less familiar ones.Basic sentences fairly accurate; complex ones have errors.Understandable, with some mispronunciation.
4Long pauses; cannot keep going without help.Basic words; frequent mistakes in word choice.Basic sentences; many errors.Often difficult to understand.

Teacher: mark the student's recording

Examiners give a whole band (0–9) for each criterion. Choose one for each; the Speaking band is calculated.

Teacher notes — lesson timing

00–05 The test in 3 parts; listen to the examiner; Task 1.
05–15 Present simple, likes and wishes (Ex 1–2); Answer + Reason + Example (Ex 3).
15–23 Vocabulary cards, Ex 4; word stress (Ex 5) — drill aloud.
23–28 Strategy for each part, cue-card notes (Ex 6), phrases (Ex 7).
28–43 Mock test with the simulator — student records the whole test.
43–60 Listen to the recording together; mark with the band guide; compare with the model script.
!

Watch for: one-word answers in Part 1; stopping after 40 seconds in Part 2; missing -s in he works; memorised answers (examiners lower the score).

Homework (about 45 minutes)

  1. Listen to the model test in Exam Script twice. Repeat 5 of Lucas's answers out loud, copying his rhythm. (15 min)
  2. Record your own answers to the 11 Part 1 questions — Answer + Reason + Example each time. (15 min)
  3. Part 2 practice: make notes for 1 minute, then speak for 2 minutes. Topic: Describe your hometown. Record it. (10 min)
  4. Learn the 12 words and say each one with the correct stress. (5 min)
